questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kazakhstan?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter A and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: Astana is the capital city of Kazakhstan.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It has borders with the Russian Federation in the north and west, _____, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan in the southwest, and China in the far east.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter T and has 12 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: It has borders with the Russian Federation in the north and west, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan in the southwest, and China in the far east.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Baikonur city has a special status because it is leased to _____ for Baikonur cosmodrome until 2050.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter R and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Regions” part of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: Baikonur city has a special status because it is leased to Russia for Baikonur cosmodrome until 2050.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Great Britain controlled _____ and feared that Russia was getting closer to its borders.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter I and has 5 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Russian Kazakhstan” part of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: Great Britain controlled India and feared that Russia was getting closer to its borders.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It attracted over $40 billion in foreign investment since _____ and accounts for some 57% of the nation's industrial output.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the 90s of the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Natural resources” part of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: It attracted over $40 billion in foreign investment since 1993 and accounts for some 57% of the nation's industrial output.
